justification: Changes what an exported, user-facing PDF asserts about a specific property: which clause it cites, whether the Housing SEPP applies, and whether the site sits in a TOD catchment. No schema or pipeline change, but wrong content in a document someone relies on is the most expensive kind of defect this codebase can ship.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_conveyancing_clause_citation.py -q && cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/components/pdf-context-claims.test.ts
falsifiable_check.fails_when: clause_ref reverts to rows[0][7] (5 of 7 Python tests fail), the Housing SEPP line goes back to testing the zone alone, the TOD line reverts to asserting the property is outside a catchment, or any SEPP reverts to a bare 'Not applicable' verdict (4 of 8 Jest tests fail). Both directions were mutation-verified by restoring the original code and watching exactly those tests go red. Two further defects were found by a GPT-5.6 cross-review of this diff and fixed before merge: an absent property.zone became 'Unknown' and rendered as a definitive 'Does not apply' verdict (the same assert-without-data defect as the TOD line, two lines away), and `dh_setbacks or sd_setbacks` skipped the secondary-dwelling list whenever any dwelling-house control existed, dropping a real citation when the dwelling-house clause was blank.

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_setback_controls via fetch_dcp_setbacks, and PropertyContext passed into ContextSection. Established by reading: the function drops rows with two `continue` guards (needs_review, and a zone_specific condition naming other zones) yet cited rows[0]; and ContextSection is passed no TOD or LMR field at all, confirmed by grepping the component for tod/TOD/lmr/LMR - zero hits.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Expected DQ-34 to be the worst thing in that table. It was not. The hardcoded TOD line is a categorical claim about the site with no data path behind it, so it could never be right for a property inside a catchment; DQ-34 at least had a correct answer half the time. Also assumed this was the conveyancing PDF - it is not. ContextSection feeds ProvisionReport, reached from the live assessment page via ProvisionsByTocStructure; the conveyancing PDF is generated in Python.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new surface. Both fixes are corrections inside existing render paths. The Housing SEPP gate reuses the heritage condition already written in determineDevelopmentPathway in the same file rather than introducing a second eligibility rule - having two was the defect.

functions.name: fetch_dcp_setbacks
functions.input: a database connection, an LGA slug and the property zone code
functions.output: the rendered setback control lists plus a clause_ref now taken from a control that survived the filters
functions.if_none: when every row is filtered out the clause reference is an empty string rather than a reference to a control the reader cannot see

values: N/A - no new business value is read; the change corrects which existing value is cited and what is claimed.

queries.purpose: select the DCP setback controls for this council, from which the cited clause is now drawn
queries.where_clause: the existing SELECT is unchanged and already scopes on lga and excludes needs_review rows; this change only alters which of the returned rows supplies clause_ref, and the per-row needs_review and zone-mismatch guards remain

break_it.scenario: The SELECT in fetch_dcp_setbacks returns rows for the council but every one is dropped by the needs_review or zone-mismatch guard, and the caller renders a setback section anyway with a dangling clause reference.
break_it.what_happens: The query is unchanged and still scopes on lga with needs_review excluded, but the per-row guards can empty both rendered lists. clause_ref is now derived from those lists, so it becomes an empty string and the section carries no citation rather than a false one.
break_it.how: test_no_citation_is_invented_when_everything_is_filtered_out drives the real function with a single needs_review row and asserts clause_ref == ''.

break_it.scenario: The PDF cites a clause that the same function deliberately suppressed because it is under review after a DCP amendment.
break_it.what_happens: clause_ref came from rows[0] of the raw query, which may be a suppressed row. Now taken from the first control that survived the filters.
break_it.how: test_leading_row_under_review_is_not_cited, run against the real function with a stubbed connection.

break_it.scenario: The PDF cites a clause that applies to a DIFFERENT zone than the property, which is worse than citing nothing.
break_it.what_happens: Same root cause; the zone-mismatch guard dropped the row from display but not from the citation.

break_it.scenario: Everything is filtered out and the code invents a reference anyway.
break_it.what_happens: Returns an empty clause_ref so the caller renders nothing. An invented citation is worse than an absent one when citation is the product claim.

break_it.scenario: A heritage property gets a PDF saying both 'DA - CDC not permitted' and 'Housing SEPP applies - eligible for CDC'.
break_it.what_happens: It did. The SEPP line tested zone only. Now gated on the same heritage condition as determineDevelopmentPathway, and a zone match reads as the zone test passing rather than an eligibility verdict.
break_it.how: Jest guards assert the old zone-only string cannot return and that the heritage check is present.

break_it.scenario: The PDF states the property is not within 400m of a metro station without ever checking.
break_it.what_happens: It was hardcoded, and the component receives no TOD data, so no input could change it. Now reports that TOD was not assessed and points at the Portal maps.
break_it.how: Jest guard asserts the hardcoded sentence is absent and the not-assessed wording is present.

break_it.scenario: Someone re-adds a bare 'Not applicable' verdict for a SEPP whose applicability depends on a proposal the report never sees.
break_it.what_happens: Four such lines shipped. The guard now fails if any reappears, and requires at least four scope-worded replacements.
break_it.how: Counts occurrences rather than checking one string, so removing three and leaving one still fails.

break_it.scenario: The source-level Jest guards trip on the explanatory comments that document the old wording, forcing the fix to be undocumented.
break_it.what_happens: Comments and JSX comment blocks are stripped before matching, so the guard asserts on what the component renders, not on prose about it.
break_it.how: Strip step covers block comments, JSX comment expressions and line comments; verified by the suite passing with the old strings quoted in comments.

break_it.scenario: A property with no zone data gets a PDF stating the Housing SEPP does not apply — a definitive negative derived from nothing.
break_it.what_happens: zoneDisplay falls back to 'Unknown', which is not in HOUSING_SEPP_ZONES, so the not-covered branch fired. Now an absent zone short-circuits to 'Not assessed - zoning data unavailable'.
break_it.how: hasZone guard ahead of the membership test; Jest asserts both the wording and the guard exist. Raised by cross-review, not by me — I had just fixed the identical class two lines below.

break_it.scenario: A rendered secondary-dwelling control carries a real clause but the PDF shows no citation, because a dwelling-house control with a blank clause existed.
break_it.what_happens: `dh_setbacks or sd_setbacks` stopped at the truthy dwelling-house list. Both lists are now searched in order.

post_merge.db_reset: None. No schema or data change.
post_merge.manual_verify: Export the provisions PDF for a heritage-listed property and confirm the SEPP table no longer says the Housing SEPP applies while the pathway says DA, and that the TOD row reads 'Not assessed in this report'. Then export for a property whose leading DCP control is under review and confirm the cited clause matches a control actually listed.
